text:
Maya (Design): Heads-up — sharing initial mocks for the 'threshold rule composer'. Curious about the signal-to-noise for the channel routing controls and whether the sample event renderer gives enough context for on-call. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE — key decisions I'm trying to land: compact row vs stacked cards for rules, and whether channel badges live in the composer or only in a separate routing panel. Quick takes?

Omar (PM): Love the direction. One ask from SRE: keep a single-line compact summary for rules in the main list so we can scan hundreds quickly. Expand for details on click.

Liam (Eng): Stacked cards = more DOM and slower list scrolling at scale. Compact row + expand is friendlier for performance. Also: avoid heavy per-row icons, they cause layout thrash on render.

Sasha (Accessibility): a11y nits: when the inline editor expands, focus order currently jumps and screen readers lose context. Suggest making the inline editor behave like a bordered region with proper keyboard focus management. Also add an `aria-live` polite region for the sample renderer so AT users know the preview updated.

Priya (Product): Copy nit — 'suppress until' is ambiguous. Recommend 'suppress notifications until' or 'mute channels until' depending on whether the action is scoped to notifications or routing. Also: if we can estimate per-rule alert volume (low/med/high), that'd help prioritization.

Evan (Design): Agree on copy. For the composer header I propose a short 'Rule name' placeholder + a tooltip (info icon) with a one-line description, instead of long inline help text that pushes layout. I added an inline token for estimated volume.

Nina (Design): For channel routing, instead of full badges inside every rule row, show a collapsed 'routing' pill with a count (e.g., "3 channels"). Clicking the pill opens a small panel with the full list and toggles. Keeps the composer tidy and reduces noise.

Liam (Eng): Implementation note: use a positioned popover for the routing panel. Ensure we set `aria-expanded` on the pill and manage focus — avoid nesting a modal inside a modal. Performance-wise this is easier than rendering the full list inline.

Sasha (Accessibility): Popover accessibility: role="dialog" with `aria-modal=false`, but trap focus while it's open; allow Escape to close and return focus to the routing pill. Also provide keyboard shortcuts to jump between the rule list and the routing popover.

Maya (Design): Thanks, good catch on focus. I also experimented with a 'sample event' voice toggle (Ops vs On-call vs Manager) to show how the notification text changes. Any objections to adding a small 'voice' selector in the sample settings?

Priya (Product): I like the voice selector — helps teams validate messaging for different audiences. Caveat: hide it behind a small 'sample settings' chevron so we don't increase surface area for new users.

Evan (Design): Contrast note: channel pills at small sizes drop below AA on several backgrounds. Instead of filled pills use a subtle border treatment for small pills. Example CSS to try: ```border: 1px solid #CED4DA; background: transparent; color: #17202A;```

Liam (Eng): Also watch channel names — people paste long names and emoji. Use `text-overflow: ellipsis` and ensure emoji are tokenized so they don't shift line height.

Maya (Design): Solid. I'll iterate with: compact row + expand on click, routing pill with popover, sample settings (voice hidden by chevron), and border-style mini-pills. Posting updated frames in a bit. Thumbs if you agree with that direction.

Priya (Product): Priya (Product): :thumbsup:

Sasha (Accessibility): Sasha (Accessibility): +1 — please add the `aria-live` note to the spec.

Liam (Eng): Liam (Eng): +1 from infra side, will prototype the popover focus behavior.

Maya (Design): Thanks all — new Figma link will be in this thread when ready.
